newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Securum says to float Castellum at 50-60 SKR/share.
newsitem.headline: Securum says to float Castellum at 50-60 SKR/share.

text.p: Swedish state-owned asset management group Securum said on Friday it would sell off 60 percent of its wholly owned property company Castellum at between 50 to 60 crowns a share.
Securum said the price would be fixed through a book-building exercise among institutional investors.
"The price range has been set at 50-60 crowns a share," Securum said in a statement. "The offer price per share in Castellum will be the same for all categories of investors."
The Swedish and international prospectuses will be published on April 24 and the institutional book-building period will run from April 28 to May 13.
The final offer price will be announced on or around May 14 and the shares are expected to be listed on the Stockholm Stock Exchange's O-list on or around May 23.
The offer involves 30 million shares or 60 percent of the share capital of Castellum.
Nordic investors are expected to be offered 18 million shares with 2.1 million going to the public.
Institutional investors are expected to be offered the remaining 12 million shares.
Securum was set up in the early 1990s to take over assets pledged by state-controlled bank Nordbanken during the country's banking crisis.
It aims to divest all assets at a reasonable price.
The Swedish government in its supplementary budget this week said it planned to wind up Securum.
